seen.extent: Four numeric cipher sheets: D/0040 one full page (about 40 lines of two- and three-digit numbers); D/0043 one full page plus one line; D/0047 about two and a half pages; D/0051 about one and a half pages. Each sheet is enclosed in a clear covering letter of Vincenzo Gonzaga to Vespasiano Gonzaga.
seen.cipher: Numbers separated by points, no interlinear decipherment on the sheets themselves. The decipherments are separate leaves filed next to them: D/0041 begins 'la voz que corria ai de que los venecianos entravan ha sido tan fija...' (Spanish), D/0045 is headed 'Guastalla julio 28 1683', D/0048 is dated 23 Aug 1685 like D/0047, and D/0054 is headed '9bre 168[3]' and is in Italian; all four are written letter by letter without word breaks, the typical look of a working decipherment, and their lengths match the cipher sheets. DARA dates D/0054 to 1684, but the leaf's own heading (November 168[3]) matches D/0051 (1683/11).

2499.note: Arnheim's edition of Luise Ulrike's unpublished letters to the Prussian royal family, vol. 2 (1747-1758, Gotha 1910; Google Books iecH_VSLsWoC, snippets through the gdata feed 16 Nov 2026), prints her letters to August Wilhelm of 1756 in clear French, with footnotes 'Chiffrebrief; nicht eigenhändig' on at least two of them (one is dated '[Stockholm], 21 mai [1756]' and begins 'Les bijoux sont arrivés hier au soir'). The ciphered letters of 1756 to August Wilhelm were thus read and printed; close as read. Confidence medium: only snippets were seen, so the match with the three letters in BPH Rep. 56 I J Nr. 23 is by writer, recipient, year and Arnheim's source (the royal house archive), not leaf by leaf.

1675.note: Not assessable yet, but nearer: Google Books snippets (gdata feed, 16 Nov 2026) show that Stein, Briefe und amtliche Schriften vol. II (1960) calendars 'Wittgenstein an Stein, Hamburg, 22. November 1808, Hausarchiv' as declining ('lehnt ... ab') a ciphered correspondence, which is the 'Ablehnung chiffrierter Briefe' of I Nr. 1,11 (a letter about cipher, not in cipher), and that an article in Nassauische Annalen 1929 prints the Wittgenstein-Stein correspondence of autumn 1808 with a note 'Chiffrierte Schreiben Steins, nur teilweise vom Empfänger aufgelöst'. So the ciphered letters of 22 Oct 1808 (I Nr. 1,16) may be Stein's letters to Wittgenstein, only partly deciphered at the time: that would make them a real open part. The 1798 Kabinettsorder (VI Nr. 2,2) has not been traced in print. Needs the Nassauische Annalen 1929 article and Stein II/2 p. 839 no. 798 opened (snippets only), or the GStA leaves.

2496.note: The GStA finding aid (read in full 11 Nov 2026) describes Rep. 64 Nr. 935 as Vrybergen's reports from the French court, Aug 1698 - Mar 1700 ('Korrespondenz, teils chiffriert') and Lubières's from Orange ('gelegentlich chiffriert'), with no decipherment noted, in a series whose cataloguer writes 'chiffriert mit Entzifferung' when a decipherment is present (Nr. 686, 695-706 and others). Japikse's Correspondentie van Willem III en van Hans Willem Bentinck, searched in full text on resources.huygens.knaw.nl on 16 Nov 2026, mentions Vrybergen and Lubières and refers to Vrybergen's letters in notes, but does not print these reports. Open as a not-online archive item, low confidence: the reports reached William III's and Portland's secretariat (Robethon sent the volume in 1707), where received cipher was normally deciphered, so interlinear decipherments may be present and unrecorded.
